lead.title: Monaco Yacht Show closes with 79 debuts and a brokerage fleet asking about USD 2.5 billion, as two yachts over 100 metres share the quay
lead.standfirst: The 35th edition, held from 23 to 26 September in Port Hercule, brought 117 superyachts and more than 560 exhibitors, and the youngest fleet the show has tracked.
lead.body: The Monaco Yacht Show closed on 26 September with a fleet that was larger, newer and more expensive than last year's. YachtBuyer, which tracks the event, counted 117 superyachts in the water against 116 in each of the two previous years, with a combined length of 5.58 kilometres and an average of 47.66 metres. The average age fell to 6.47 years from 7.28 in 2025, and 79 of the yachts were making a show debut. Forty-six had been delivered in 2026 alone. The headline pair were both owned by the game developer Gabe Newell, who acquired the Dutch yard Oceanco in 2025: the 111 metre Leviathan, delivered in November 2025 and making her first show appearance, and the rebuilt 93 metre Draak, a former charter yacht, berthed alongside. Among charter yachts the most discussed was the 102.4 metre Lürssen Nixie, delivered in June 2026, with a 270 square metre beach club and a Caribbean season ahead. Other debuts included the 80 metre Pangea, the first Amels 80 to be shown, the 72 metre Sanlorenzo Silver Fox, the yard's new flagship, and the 67.55 metre CRN Amor à Vida, the builder's first hybrid-propulsion superyacht. The commercial side was just as striking. Seventy yachts were offered for sale, up from 69 in 2025 and 65 in 2024, with total asking prices of about USD 2.5 billion and an average of USD 35.2 million. The three most expensive listings together asked EUR 415 million: the 72 metre Feadship Vanish at EUR 148 million, the 76.5 metre Feadship Boardwalk V at EUR 135 million and the 74 metre Amels Synthesis, freshly refitted, at EUR 132 million. The 75 metre Blohm+Voss Zeus, at EUR 77 million, returned to the brokerage market for the first time in almost a decade. The show itself is changing shape. A new Designer Gallery replaced the former Yacht Design and Innovation Hub, an Adventure Area gathered around 70 tenders, water toys and cars on a third quay, and a Blue Wake environmental programme counted 60 validated exhibitors. The organisers have confirmed that the 36th edition will run from 22 to 25 September 2027.
lead.why: For the person running a yacht programme or advising the family that owns one, Monaco is where charter availability, refit schedules and brokerage prices are read in a single week, and a younger fleet with more hybrid propulsion changes what the captain and the shore team need to know.

articles.title: Household staff pay is closing in on senior corporate salaries, with confidentiality adding 15 to 20 per cent, Morgan & Mallet's Beyond the Butler report finds
articles.body:
The family staffing agency Morgan & Mallet summarises the state of its market in six words in its Beyond the Butler 2025/26 report: demand is up and supply is down. Pay for the senior roles is now approaching that of senior corporate positions. In the United States, which pays the most for 60 per cent of all household roles, private chefs can reach USD 300,000, chiefs of staff USD 300,000, estate managers USD 250,000 and executive assistants USD 250,000. In the United Arab Emirates, compensation is expected to reach USD 120,000 to USD 140,000 as demand grows.

The report ties the pressure to how families now live. They are buying property in more countries, partly because of geopolitical uncertainty and looser monetary policy, and the end of non-dom status has pushed many families out of Britain towards Florida, Dubai and Switzerland. Estate managers account for 10 per cent of all requests in the United States, and the average tenure of a placement is about three years. In Britain, Brexit has made it harder for European citizens to work in households, which has pushed salaries up.

Privacy is priced explicitly. Confidentiality can raise pay by 15 to 20 per cent, and in Los Angeles 77 per cent of personal assistant roles require a non-disclosure agreement. Some households ban social media altogether and ask staff to hand over their phones on arrival. Technology is the other new requirement: in San Francisco, 83 per cent of positions recruited in the past year required comfort with integrated home systems, and staff typically need 8 to 12 weeks to adapt to a new household's set-up.

Nannies show the reverse pattern. Britain has the highest demand, at nearly a quarter of all placements, and worldwide nanny placements have a 96 per cent success rate, with candidates typically bringing six years of experience and first-aid training. Governesses are rare but in demand in Dubai and Saudi Arabia, and domestic couples remain among the most requested roles in Europe and the United States, at 21 per cent of top requests in France.
articles.why: The report sets out what a candidate is paid for: discretion, a command of home technology and the ability to run several properties, not formal credentials alone.

articles.title: Ninety-one heirs inherited a record USD 297.8 billion in a year, UBS finds, and USD 6.9 trillion will change hands by 2040
articles.body:
UBS's Billionaire Ambitions report, published on 4 December 2025, counted nearly 3,000 billionaires, up 8.8 per cent from 2,682, with total wealth at a record USD 15.8 trillion. Self-made billionaires added USD 386.5 billion, the second-highest annual increase in the report's history, and 196 new self-made names joined the list.

The transfer of wealth is the part of the report that matters most to household and family office staff. Ninety-one heirs inherited USD 297.8 billion, 36 per cent more than a year earlier. Multi-generational billionaires rose to about 860 from 805, controlling USD 4.7 trillion against USD 4.2 trillion. By 2040, roughly USD 6.9 trillion is expected to pass between generations, with at least USD 5.9 trillion going to children.

The survey, the eleventh edition, ran from 10 July to 25 September 2025. It found North America the top investment destination, named by 63 per cent of respondents, followed by Western Europe at 40 per cent and Greater China at 34 per cent.
articles.why: A change of generation often means a change of households, advisers and expectations, and whoever serves the family through a succession is working with new decision makers who may live very differently.

articles.title: Impressionist art rose 13.6 per cent in 2025 while whisky fell 10.9 per cent, as Knight Frank's luxury index slipped 0.4 per cent
articles.body: Knight Frank's Wealth Report, published on 23 April 2026, gives a clear picture of what collectors held and what they sold. Its Luxury Investment Index fell 0.4 per cent over 2025, but the categories moved in opposite directions. Impressionist art rose 13.6 per cent and watches rose 5.1 per cent, while classic cars fell 3.7 per cent and whisky fell 10.9 per cent. The year also produced a record for a modern work at auction: Klimt's Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer sold for USD 236.4 million. The same report found that high net worth individuals and family offices deployed USD 464 billion into commercial real estate in 2025, against USD 347 billion from institutional investors.
articles.why: A household that holds art, watches, cars and a cellar needs someone who knows which of those markets is rising, because insurance values, storage and the timing of any sale all follow the cycle.
articles.src: Family Wealth Report, citing Knight Frank

briefs.b: The Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show runs from 28 October to 1 November across seven venues, with superyachts over 100 feet moored at the 17th Street Yacht Basin. Serious buyers are advised to arrange access through brokers or exhibitors in advance.
Baglietto showed the T60 in Monaco, a 60 metre yacht of about 1,100 GT and the largest the yard has built, alongside the 50 metre FAST50 with a 30-knot top speed. Both were world premieres.
An AI robot on the Oceanco deck waved to visitors and drew wide attention on social media, and more than 560 brands exhibited in total. The 2027 show is set for 22 to 25 September.
